read_sources: one completed non-Mal blind literary proposal for format only

non_authority_statement: Candidate literary and disputation-form evidence only. Every unit is LOW confidence and deferred_human_or_external_ai. No theology, priesthood doctrine, marriage or divorce doctrine, messenger or Elijah identity, history, chronology, fulfillment, canon, authorship, preferred witness, preferred reading, preferred translation, source tradition, graph, retrieval, reviewed-gold, chunk-output, or promotion authority is claimed.
routing_principle: Prefer complete assertion/wa-amartem-style response/answer/oracle parents, stable audience and command sequences, accusation catalogues through closure, explicit oracle answers, and paired closing commands. Cross English chapter boundaries when question-answer form requires it; never use a chapter fallback.

versification_awareness.hebrew_english_difference_noted: English Mal.4.1-Mal.4.6 is commonly numbered as continuation Mal.3.19-Mal.3.24 in Hebrew versification

macro_parent_alternatives.preservation_reason: The one burden heading governs successive assertion-objection-answer disputations and closes with paired remember/behold sayings; this is literary evidence only, not authorship or canon judgment.

macro_parent_alternatives.form: opening love and honor/priest disputation complex
macro_parent_alternatives.preservation_reason: The opening love claim and name-honor dispute progress from Israel-wide assertion to a sustained priestly accusation and command, with repeated saying and name formulas.
Communal treachery accusations and the wearied-words justice question form adjacent disputes, the second crossing the English chapter edge into its arrival and judgment answer.
Return and robbery objections resolve in imperative-promises; harsh-words objections resolve through remembered fearers and the coming-day contrast across the English chapter edge.
Remember and behold introduce two compact closing sayings joined by command, day, turning, and terminal curse language.

global_hot_zones.issue: The burden superscription can stand alone or accompany the first assertion-objection-answer exchange.
global_hot_zones.handling: Keep it with the first dispute for coherence while preserving Mal.1.1 as an alternative; infer no authorship or canon claim.

global_hot_zones.issue: The English chapter edge falls inside a stable priestly address that changes from accusation to explicit command.
global_hot_zones.handling: Preserve the complete priestly dispute and record 1:6-14 and 2:1-9 alternatives; no chapter fallback.

global_hot_zones.issue: One-father questions and the this-again accusation may be two units, while difficult wording in 2:15-16 can tempt doctrinal or preferred-reading decisions.
global_hot_zones.handling: Retain both under repeated treachery and why/because form; decide no marriage/divorce doctrine, witness, reading, or translation.

global_hot_zones.issue: The accusation and justice question precede their answer across the English chapter boundary.
global_hot_zones.handling: Require the whole question-to-answer parent; do not isolate 2:17 or decide messenger identity, chronology, or fulfillment.

global_hot_zones.issue: How-shall-we-return is followed by a nested how-have-we-robbed exchange, making one or two disputes plausible.
global_hot_zones.handling: Prefer the larger return-response parent while recording smaller alternatives; infer no stewardship or blessing doctrine.

global_hot_zones.issue: The harsh-words dispute moves through counter-community, memory book, discernment, and a for-behold day oracle across the English chapter edge.
global_hot_zones.handling: Preserve the accusation-to-resolution parent; decide no history, chronology, judgment system, or fulfillment.

global_hot_zones.issue: English Malachi 4:4-6 corresponds to final verses of Hebrew chapter 3 in a common Hebrew versification convention.
global_hot_zones.handling: Record coordinate awareness only; use canonical English refs for this artifact and select no preferred witness, numbering, reading, or tradition.

global_hot_zones.issue: The proper name and before-the-day saying invite identity and fulfillment claims.
global_hot_zones.handling: Treat behold/send/turn/lest only as literary closure markers; defer identity and fulfillment completely.

units.title: Burden heading and the love disputation
units.literary_form: book-level burden superscription followed by assertion, quoted objection, comparative answer, and future confession
units.deciding_marker: The burden heading introduces the word-event; I-have-loved-you is challenged by yet-you-say how, answered through the Jacob-Esau and Edom contrast, and closed by your-eyes-will-see and you-will-say.
units.rejected_alternative: Isolating the one-verse heading, splitting the Edom counterclaim from its answer, or attaching the priestly address at 1:6.
units.defensible_basis: Burden formula, assertion/wa-amartem-style objection, answer, counterclaim and reversal, and terminal seeing/saying response make a complete opening movement.

units.title: Priests challenged, commanded, and contrasted with Levi
units.literary_form: extended priestly disputation with honor analogy, two quoted objections, defective-offering catalogue, chapter-crossing command, covenant contrast, and therefore verdict
units.deciding_marker: The father/master analogy addresses priests who despise the name; how-have-we-despised and how-have-we-polluted receive offering evidence, before now-you-priests-this-command continues the same audience through Levi contrast and a therefore conclusion.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at the chapter boundary, splitting the offering accusation from command consequences, or deciding priesthood or covenant doctrine.
units.defensible_basis: Stable priestly audience, repeated name/table/offering vocabulary, question-answer form, explicit command continuation, if-then warning, ideal-versus-you contrast, and therefore close support the cross-chapter parent.

units.title: One-father questions and the treachery disputation
units.literary_form: communal rhetorical questions, treachery accusation, this-again-you-do sequel, quoted why objection, witness answer, and guard-your-spirit refrain
units.deciding_marker: One-father and one-creator questions begin communal we discourse; treacherously repeats through accusations, this-again-you-do introduces tears at the altar, yet-you-say-why receives an answer, and repeated guard-your-spirit closes the movement.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting 2:10-12 from 2:13-16 without preserving their treachery link, or making marriage/divorce doctrine or a preferred rendering of difficult clauses.
units.defensible_basis: Audience shift to communal we, repeated treachery vocabulary, second-accusation marker, quoted objection and because answer, and closing refrain provide a complete disputation parent.

units.title: Where is justice? Messenger, refining, and swift-witness answer
units.literary_form: accusation and quoted objection answered by a cross-chapter arrival oracle, endurance questions, refining sequence, and judgment catalogue
units.deciding_marker: You-have-wearied opens the accusation; how-have-we-wearied and where-is-the-God-of-justice state the dispute, then behold-I-send and suddenly-come answer through who-can-endure questions, refining of offerings, and I-will-come-near-to-judgment with a witness catalogue.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at the chapter boundary, separating 3:1-4 from 3:5, or deciding messenger identity, fulfillment, chronology, or priesthood theology.
units.defensible_basis: Direct accusation/wa-amartem objection, explicit justice question, behold answer, coming/refining progression, then-offering result, and judgment/witness closure require preservation across the English chapter edge.

units.title: Return, robbery questions, and storehouse-test oracle
units.literary_form: return disputation containing a nested robbery question-answer, imperative test, promise catalogue, and nations declaration
units.deciding_marker: The unchanging/therefore statement leads to return-to-me and how-shall-we-return; will-a-man-rob and how-have-we-robbed extend the answer into tithes and offerings, followed by bring-and-test imperatives, promise clauses, and all-nations-shall-call-you-blessed closure.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting at 3:8 as though the robbery exchange were unrelated to how-to-return, or turning the unit into doctrine or authorization.
units.defensible_basis: Return inclusio, two linked objection formulas, accusation evidence, imperative response, repeated future answer clauses, and terminal nations/land saying support one full parent.

units.title: Harsh words, remembered fearers, and the coming-day contrast
units.literary_form: final disputation with quoted protest catalogue, counter-community report, memory-book response, discernment saying, and cross-chapter day oracle
units.deciding_marker: Your-words-have-been-harsh is challenged by what-have-we-spoken; the vain-to-serve catalogue is answered by then-those-who-feared, listening and a memory book, then-you-shall-discern, and for-behold-the-day resolves the proud/wicked and name-fearing contrast through in-the-day-that-I-make.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at either chapter boundary, detaching the fearers response from the accusation, or deciding judgment chronology, fulfillment, or theological identity.
units.defensible_basis: Accusation/wa-amartem objection, quoted complaint, then/then/for-behold progression, repeated fear/name/serve/wicked vocabulary, and shared day-that-I-make refrain bind the cross-chapter resolution.

units.title: Remember Moses; behold the sent prophet
units.literary_form: two-part epilogue with remembrance command, sending announcement, turning purpose, and lest-I-come curse close
units.deciding_marker: Remember opens a command concerning statutes and ordinances; behold-I-will-send adds a before-the-day announcement whose he-will-turn purpose ends in a lest-I-come-and-strike clause.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating the remembrance and sending sayings without preserving their paired closure, or identifying Elijah, selecting fulfillment, or preferring Hebrew/English numbering.
units.defensible_basis: Paired imperative and behold formulas, all-Israel and day language, purpose clause, reciprocal hearts pattern, and terminal conditional curse make a formal book closure.

required_evidence_for_challenge: text-internal disputation, audience, command, oracle, catalogue, or closure marker
